sub_questions: How can the Himalayan Disaster Atlas improve even more overall — which improvements matter most, and in what order?
How can the daily copy of official DHM, BIPAD and NEMRC data become more reliable, more complete and more useful (feed reliability, new official sources, history, freshness)?
How can the MapLibre map and its place search improve (layers, hazard data, search coverage, Nepali names, performance)?
How can the hypothetical flood and GLOF scenario models improve scientifically (hydraulic routing, dam-breach, inventories, validation, uncertainty)?
How can the hypothetical earthquake scenario model improve scientifically (GMPEs, site effects, rupture models, exposure, damage/loss, validation)?
How can the site better serve Nepali users — bilingual EN/NE content, Nepali names, accessibility, low bandwidth, mobile, offline, literacy, dissemination channels?
How can the printable scenario reports and the static public site be made more useful and trustworthy for decision makers (risk communication, disclaimers, provenance)?
How can the project increase its real-world impact (users, partners such as DHM/NDRRMA/ICIMOD, adoption, sustainability, open data, governance)?
Which hazards or capabilities are missing entirely (e.g. landslides, early-warning integration, multi-hazard, climate projections) and are they worth adding?

entities.name: Himalayan Disaster Atlas (the project as a whole)
DHM (Department of Hydrology and Meteorology) official data
BIPAD (NDRRMA disaster information portal) official data
NEMRC (National Earthquake Monitoring and Research Center) official data
Nepali district names from the constitution

required_formats: prioritised list / roadmap of improvements (the question is 'how can this improve')
required_sections: A prioritised recommendation section answering 'how can this project improve even more'
required_section_headings: ## 2. Official Data Feeds: DHM, BIPAD and NEMRC
## 6. Serving Nepali Users: Language, Access and Reach
## 7. Printable Reports, Trust and Risk Communication
scope_conditions: Nepal (with transboundary Himalayan context where it affects Nepal, e.g. GLOFs from Tibet)
the project must stay a static, public, read-only, free website with no credentials in the browser (current architecture constraint, evaluate trade-offs if recommending otherwise)
scenarios are hypothetical model runs, not forecasts or warnings; official agencies remain authoritative
improvements across all facets: data, science, usability, accessibility, reliability, impact

levers.domain_notes: Sourcing: peer-reviewed hazard science (GLOF modelling, Nepal GMPEs/site response, flood routing), official Nepali agency documentation (DHM, NDRRMA/BIPAD, NEMRC, ICIMOD), and evaluations of risk-communication and early-warning platforms (UNDRR, WMO, World Bank, Practical Action, peer platforms). Strong evidence is measured validation against observed events (e.g. 2015 Gorkha, 2021 Melamchi, 2023-2024 GLOFs) and evaluated user studies; vendor or project self-description is weak. Recency: data-source and platform facts within ~24 months; science may be older if still standard.

rationale.register: query asks how a project can improve — evaluation/recommendation-shaped, but no explicit 'should we'; ambiguous between analyze and advocate, so default analyze with low confidence
rationale.inference_depth: open literature on Nepal hazards and early warning is rich; agency API documentation may be thin — revisit at loci analysis
